topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the course structure, learning outcomes, and foundational themes for the lecture.

topics.label: Biological basis and experimental modeling of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as a progressive failure of normal differentiation and tissue architecture driven by molecular changes, along with experimental models used to study tumor biology.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical and histological distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, the process of tissue invasion across basement membranes, and the stepwise progression to metastatic disease.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard naming rules and exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumors according to their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the anatomical and physiological processes through which primary and metastatic tumors disrupt normal organ function to cause illness and death.

topics.label: Epidemiology and comparative incidence of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the patterns, frequency, and mortality of cancer types across human populations and other animal species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the principles, diagnostic methods, and relative efficacy of screening programs designed to detect pre-malignant and malignant lesions.

topics.label: Conclusion and closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic reviews the learning outcomes and provides logistical reminders for upcoming practicals and lectures.
